name: Sharjah Heritage Museum
short: Traditional Emirati life, crafts and customs inside a restored family house.
description: Set in the Heart of Sharjah heritage district, the Sharjah Heritage Museum occupies Bait Al Naboodah, a coral-stone family house built in the 1840s. Its rooms open onto a shaded courtyard, a design that kept families cool long before air conditioning. Galleries cover the full cycle of Emirati life: birth and childhood, traditional medicine, poetry and storytelling, pearl diving, and the crafts that sustained coastal communities. Look out for the original wind tower, the carved teak doors and the hand-woven sadu textiles.

name: Al Noor Mosque
short: An Ottoman-style mosque on the Khalid Lagoon, open to visitors for guided tours.
description: Inspired by the Blue Mosque in Istanbul, Al Noor Mosque sits on the Khobaib corniche overlooking the Khalid Lagoon. Its central dome, slender twin minarets and limestone walls glow at night when the mosque is lit. Visitors can join guided tours that explain Islamic customs and the mosque's architecture. Modest dress is required, and abayas and headscarves are provided at the entrance.

name: Museum of Islamic Civilization
short: Over 5,000 artefacts covering Islamic science, art and faith under a golden dome.
description: Housed in a former souq on the Corniche, the Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilization displays more than 5,000 artefacts from across the Islamic world. Galleries are devoted to faith, science and technology, and the decorative arts, from astrolabes and early medical instruments to ceramics, calligraphy and textiles. Don't miss the central dome, decorated with a mosaic of the zodiac.

name: Sharjah Art Museum
short: The region's largest art museum, with Orientalist works and modern Arab art.
description: Sharjah Art Museum is one of the largest art museums in the Gulf. Its permanent collection includes Orientalist paintings and maps from the Barjeel and ruler's collections, alongside modern and contemporary works by Arab artists. Rotating exhibitions are hosted throughout the year, many linked to the Sharjah Biennial.

name: Al Hisn Sharjah
short: The 1820s fort that was once home to the ruling family, now a museum.
description: Built around 1820, Al Hisn Sharjah was the seat of the ruling Al Qasimi family and the emirate's first line of defence. The fort was almost entirely demolished in 1969, then carefully rebuilt using original materials and reopened as a museum. Inside, exhibits trace the history of the ruling family, the town's trade and the fort's own story, including a restored prison cell and the original wooden gate.
location: Al Hisn Avenue, Heart of Sharjah

name: Al Majaz Waterfront
short: Lagoon-side parks, dancing fountains and cafés, best at sunset.
description: Al Majaz Waterfront stretches along the Khalid Lagoon with landscaped gardens, a children's play area, walking paths and a row of restaurants and cafés. In the evening the Sharjah Fountain puts on a music and light show over the water. Come at sunset for views of Al Noor Mosque across the lagoon.
